You are called a "specialist" in words, but you are a "generalist" in practice. I will come to you for all matters big and small.

paragraphs: 6/10 Explain that HR is a "medium-to-high exposure" profession: transactional tasks such as screening, scheduling, and statistics are being largely taken over by AI. Pure process-based HR is risky, but people are still needed to identify people, communicate, and make business and organizational judgments. The position is transforming into HRBP.

Medium and high exposure must transform: stop just doing the work of "screening resumes and doing onboarding", move into HRBP, organizational development, and talent management, use AI as an efficiency tool, and spend time on the high-value aspects of understanding business and dealing with people.

You can major in human resources, psychology, or management, but the key is internship: during college, work as an intern in a corporate HR department or a recruitment agency to familiarize yourself with the recruitment process; at the same time, learn some data analysis. In the future, HR will increasingly look at data.

Go to HRBP and expert positions: Understand the business in depth, make recruitment, compensation, and organizational development professional; use AI tools to improve efficiency, leave time for business dialogue and employee communication, and don’t get stuck in affairs.

There are advantages to switching from administration, sales, and operations to HR: you can supplement your knowledge of recruitment and labor law, with a focus on communication and judgment. During the interview, you emphasize that you can "read people" and tell a case in which you read people accurately and handled conflicts.

The HR team should be layered: hand over transactional work to ATS and AI, and let HR focus on the role of business partner; design a "recruitment → HRBP" growth path for employees, and use business rotation to cultivate HR who understand the business.
